title: Tune-A-Video: One-Shot Tuning of Image Diffusion Models for Text-to-Video Generation
grouping: Two side-by-side sections split by a thin vertical rule, titled 'Fine-Tuning' and 'Inference' in large plain sans type. In Fine-Tuning, the denoising network sits in a rounded container labelled 'x T steps'; a blue-tinted strip at the container's bottom, joined by dotted zoom lines to one attention column, expands the attention block into four rounded sub-blocks (ST-Attn, Cross-Attn, FFN, T-Attn). A four-entry legend (Conv Block, Attn Block, Updated, Frozen) sits beside the container. Inference is a small clockwise loop: video -> DDIM inversion -> noise -> denoising -> edited video.
shapes_depth: Every video tensor (clean, noised, edited) is an offset stack of about six square frames, photographs or grey noise. Process steps (diffusion, DDIM inversion, denoising) are tall rounded pills with rotated text. The network is drawn as pairs of thin vertical rounded columns whose height shrinks to the middle and grows back (grey = conv, light blue = attention), with dashed skip arrows across the top. Inside the zoomed attention blocks, each projection is a small square split into Q (orange) over KV (grey). Text prompts are set in a handwritten italic face in quotes; a long arrow labelled 'Reconstruction Loss' in italic runs over the top from input to output.
proposed_highlight: Trainable parts are shown only by colour: orange Q boxes (Updated) versus grey KV boxes (Frozen) in the zoomed attention strip, keyed in the legend. In Inference, the edited words of the prompt are coloured blue while the unchanged words stay black.
lesson: Draw every video tensor - clean, noised, edited - as the same offset stack of frames so the noise and editing stages read as changes to one clip, and mark which projections are trained inside the zoomed attention blocks with an orange/grey Q|KV split keyed by a short legend.
notes: Venue ICCV from Semantic Scholar title match; year = arXiv preprint year (2212.11565).

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.task: one-shot tuning of T2I diffusion for text-to-video

core.what: two panels split by a vertical rule: a wide 'Fine-Tuning' panel on the left (skiing video -> diffusion xT -> noise -> U-Net -> reconstructed video, with a Reconstruction Loss line over the top) and a narrower 'Inference' panel on the right (same video -> DDIM inversion -> noise -> denoising with a new prompt -> Spider-Man video)

relations.form: large titles 'Fine-Tuning' and 'Inference' head two side-by-side panels separated by a thin vertical line, the same source clip starting both
fine-tuning reads left to right along one line of frame stacks and boxes; inference runs right through DDIM inversion to a noise stack, then down and back left through denoising to the edited clip
blue dotted lines drop from one attention block of the U-Net into a blue panel below it showing ST-Attn, Cross-Attn, FFN and T-Attn, each attention split into a Q cell and a KV cell
a line leaves the input video, runs over the whole panel and drops into the reconstructed video, labelled 'Reconstruction Loss'
the prompt 'A man is skiing' sends a line along the bottom and up into the Cross-Attn KV cell; at inference the new prompt enters the denoising box from below
'xT steps' labels above the diffusion box, the U-Net frame and DDIM inversion stand for the repeated denoising

channels.colour: orange = updated parameters (every Q cell), light grey = frozen (KV cells, FFN), light blue = attention blocks - keyed; but grey also fills the Conv Block glyph, so grey carries both 'conv block' and 'frozen'; blue text in the inference prompt = edited words
channels.shape: stacked frames = video clips; noise stacks = latents; tall capsules = U-Net blocks (grey conv, blue attention, keyed); rounded boxes = processes
channels.line: solid black arrows = data flow; dashed arrows inside the U-Net = skip connections; blue dotted lines = zoom tie
channels.frame: a rounded frame = the U-Net; a blue rounded panel = the opened transformer block

quality.strengths: what is trained is drawn at the finest grain - inside the opened attention block only the Q cells are orange, so the reader sees that the method updates query projections and leaves the rest frozen; data are real (the skiing clip, noise stacks, the edited Spider-Man clip and quoted prompts) and the two phases share the source clip so their difference is visible
quality.weaknesses: grey means both convolution block and frozen parameter; the reconstruction-loss line runs over the top of the entire panel and the prompt line along its bottom, each with right-angle bends; the inference path turns back on itself (right, down, left), so its output lands to the left of its input

insights.structure: Two sections split by a thin vertical rule, titled 'Fine-Tuning' (wide, left) and 'Inference' (narrow, right); the fine-tuning U-Net container has a blue strip zooming one attention column into ST-Attn, Cross-Attn, FFN, T-Attn.
insights.data: Every video is an offset stack of about six frames (real ski photos or grey noise); the prompt is a handwritten quote; Q and KV projections are small split squares, orange when updated, grey when frozen.
insights.emphasis: Orange 'Updated' vs grey 'Frozen' fill marks exactly which projections are tuned; the edited prompt words are blue in the inference half.
insights.flow: Fine-tuning reads left to right video -> diffusion -> noise -> U-Net -> video, with a 'Reconstruction Loss' line arching over the top; inference is a clockwise loop DDIM inversion -> noise -> denoising -> edited video.
insights.avoid: The prompt line in Fine-Tuning runs along the bottom and up into Cross-Attn through the zoomed inset, a long route that is easy to miss.

arrangement.units: two unframed sections Fine-Tuning and Inference, separated by a vertical rule, each with a large title
arrangement.inputs_as: a stack of real video frames with a quoted prompt below
arrangement.losses_at: reconstruction loss as a line arching over the top of the fine-tuning section
arrangement.shared: the same video drawn as input in both sections
